brief.text:
GANGSTAS PARADISE (Sleeper) — Zay Flowers reversal: missed BOTH Wednesday and Thursday practice, Friday's session (today) decides Sunday
Do now: nothing to click yet, but watch your phone — yesterday's read had Flowers trending toward a full return; that was wrong. He's now missed back-to-back practices with the hamstring and Ravens coach Jesse Minter still calls him day-to-day. If Friday's report shows him limited or DNP, plan to start Josh Downs instead. Separately, Chase Brown's handcuff Samaje Perine (knee, DNP Thursday) is banged up — doesn't touch Brown's own start (he's fully healthy), just a heads up for waiver planning Tuesday.
Locks next 24h: none — every rostered player kicks off Sunday or later.
Lineup: only real change is Flowers moving from "start" to "watch" pending today's practice report — everyone else on the roster is fully healthy and unchanged from Tuesday. Chase Brown and Higgins still grind on volume against Houston's #1 defense (22.0 implied), both full practice participants all week. Tuten and Chris Rodriguez remain a real committee in Jacksonville but nothing new there — Tuten still the start. Aubrey remains the week's best matchup at K, home vs Washington, and the line moved further Dallas' way (27.5 implied).

GAME OF THROWS (Yahoo) — still no fresh screenshot, a 6th straight run on the same Week 1 file from 2026-09-13, now 5 days stale
Do now: same ask as every run this week — drop a Week 1 final box score AND a live Week 2 matchup screenshot into the War room folder. Still working off public schedule and Vegas lines only, not your actual live roster or score.
Locks next 24h: none
Lineup (best-effort, unconfirmed roster): no changes from Tuesday's call. Pickens is still the week's best play on this roster (home vs Washington, line now 27.5 implied). Judkins remains the confirmed lead Browns back at Tampa Bay — his own backup Dylan Sampson landed on IR this week (Raheim Sanders now RB2), which doesn't touch Judkins' role, but Sunday's forecast now confirms real thunderstorms and a 103° heat index in Tampa, worth a game-flow watch. Myers' game got a notch tougher: Sam Darnold is OUT for Seattle (glute), Drew Lock starts, and the total dropped to 41.5 — still start him, just temper expectations. Washington's role stays flat — Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr. (shoulder) still limited but still expected to play, unchanged from earlier in the week.
Waivers / trades: not a waiver day — see the Waivers/Trades tabs for the standing boards, unchanged since Tuesday.

FYI: Chase Brown again starts in both leagues against Houston's #1 defense, fully healthy in both spots. Alvin Kamara looked like a full Wednesday participant and is trending back for New Orleans, which touches Etienne's game script more than his role. Four total RB-room shakeups this week worth knowing: Perine (CIN, Brown's backup) and Sampson (CLE, Judkins' old backup) both banged up/on IR.

waivers.text:
SLEEPER — same board as Tuesday since none of last week's targets have been claimed yet. TE depth is still your #1 problem (Strange is your only rostered TE and shares Week 7's bye cluster with Herbert, Hampton, and your DEF), and Chase Brown insurance still matters since he starts in BOTH your leagues. FAAB: $93 left (spent $7 on Kmet/Vele/Shough claims already), waiver position 11 of 12 — doesn't matter much under FAAB, just get bids in before Wednesday's clear.
1. Samaje Perine (RB, CIN) — still unclaimed, still the direct Chase Brown handcuff anchoring your RB1 slot in both leagues. Drop Michael Wilson (WR, buried behind Marvin Harrison Jr./Trey McBride in ARI). FAAB $14.
2. Mike Gesicki (TE, CIN) — still available, still the best TE upgrade on the wire and it solves your zero-depth problem outright. Cincinnati's bye (Week 6) doesn't overlap Strange's Week 7. Drop Cole Kmet (TE, no clear role in CHI's rotation). FAAB $16.
3. Kimani Vidal (RB, LAC) — direct committee-mate to your own Omarion Hampton; cheap bye/injury insurance on a player who's already your RB1. Drop Woody Marks (RB, buried in Houston's committee). FAAB $8.
4. Evan Engram (TE, DEN) — fallback if you miss on Gesicki, or a second TE for bye coverage (Denver's bye is Week 10, different from both Strange's Week 7 and Gesicki's Week 6). No fixed drop unless you land both TEs — then cut whichever bench piece you value least. FAAB $6.
5. Devin Singletary (RB, NYG) — speculative depth add only if you whiff on the RBs above; lowest priority. No fixed drop, conditional pickup. FAAB $3.
No DEF/K stream needed this week — Aubrey and the Jaguars D/ST both carry playable Week 2 matchups per the Analysis tab.

trades.text:
SLEEPER — send Tyler Shough (New Orleans' actual Week 1 starting QB, currently buried as your QB2 behind Herbert) to Emeka Eggbucock ("Emeka Eggbucock") for Kaelon Black (RB, SF). Their starter Kyler Murray is in the concussion protocol — still day-to-day as of this run, with Carson Wentz starting if he can't go — and they're carrying zero backup QB, so a hot streaming starter has real short-term value to them. They're deep at RB (Ashton Jeanty, Tony Pollard, Javonte Williams, and Black all rostered), so Black is a fair piece to deal from that surplus. For you, Black is a legitimate stash: he out-touched Christian McCaffrey in the second half of Week 1 (15 total touches, tied for the team lead) and Draft Sharks already has him "pulling away" in San Francisco's RB2 race — real insurance and potential standalone value behind a back the 49ers want to manage carefully after a 450-touch 2025. This directly fixes your thinnest bench spot (Woody Marks, a committee back in Houston, is your only other RB depth) without touching Stefon Diggs, who's still starting regardless of the Flowers situation. Checked Weeks 15-17 first: moving a buried backup QB for a real RB stash only helps your playoff bench, it doesn't cost you anything there. Offer hasn't been accepted yet as of this run — still pending.

YAHOO — no trade idea this run. Still no visibility into other managers' rosters or trade blocks in your private Yahoo league (screenshots only cover your own team and the current matchup), so I can't responsibly name a real deal. No trade.txt found in the War room folder either.

season.lesson: Started Josh Downs (5.7) over Stefon Diggs sitting on the bench (15.5) in the flex — 9.8 points left on the table. Separately, Zay Flowers' 26-point day ended in a hamstring re-injury that's now clouding Week 2; watch practice reports closely on players who leave games early even when the box score looks great.
